operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated analytics on comments across the platform.

This endpoint provides system administrators and platform analysts with high-level insights into comment activity trends without exposing individual comment content. The operation returns comprehensive summary metrics including total comment count, counts by author role (citizen/administrator/superAdministrator), counts by section, average comments per article, and distribution by time period.

The response is structured for dashboard visualization and long-term trend analysis. It enables administrators to identify patterns such as spikes in comment volume, disproportionate activity in specific sections, or changes in user engagement demographics. All responses are anonymized aggregates - no individual comment content, author identifiers, or raw text fields are returned to maintain user privacy and comply with data protection regulations.

This endpoint does not support pagination since response is a single summary object, not a list. Filtering parameters are applied via query string parameters including startDate, endDate, sectionId, and authorRole. Data is sourced from the economic_board_comments table and joined with economic_board_citizens, economic_board_administrators, and economic_board_super_administrators tables to determine author role. Article section affiliation is obtained via join with economic_board_articles and economic_board_sections.

This operation does not modify any data and is read-only. It does not return metadata about individual comments to prevent reconstruction of user behavior patterns that could compromise privacy.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query economic_board_comments table and join with economic_board_citizens, economic_board_administrators, and economic_board_super_administrators to classify author roles. Join with economic_board_articles to link comments to sections. Group by author role and section. Calculate total count, average per article, and time-based distributions. Use postgreSQL aggregate functions (COUNT, AVG, EXTRACT for time periods). Return single JSON object with aggregated metrics: totalComments, commentsByRole, commentsBySection, averageCommentsPerArticle, trendByDay. Do not return individual comment records. Do not include any user identifiers or raw content.

responseBody.description: Aggregated comment analytics summary containing total counts, role distribution, section distribution, average per article, and trend data.

operations.specification:
Query economic_board_articles table for articles flagged for moderation (based on content analysis matching dialectic extremism keywords from 07-admin-system.md).

- Use GIN full-text search on title and content fields with a predefined list of extremist keywords.
- Filter articles where deleted_at IS NULL (only active articles).
- Ensure no duplicate results using DISTINCT ON article_id.
- Return results with pagination: 20 items per page, cursor-based pagination for performance.
- Include the auto-generated moderation flag reason from system analysis in response.
- JOIN with economic_board_citizens to retrieve author display_name.
- Do NOT join with sections unless absolutely necessary for performance.
- Sort results by created_at DESC to show newest flagged content first.
- Implement rate limiting: 10 requests per minute per admin.
- No session management required as authentication is enforced at the API gateway by role check.
- Cache results for 5 minutes to reduce database load on repeated requests.
- Exclude articles with existing 'moderated' or 'rejected' records in audit logs if such a model existed, though no separate moderation log table is provided in schema.
operations.description:
Retrieve a list of articles that have been automatically flagged for human moderation review.

This endpoint provides administrators with a curated list of economic or political discussion articles that have been flagged by the system's automated content moderation engine. Articles are flagged based on the presence of keywords or patterns associated with dialectic extremism, hate speech, or other policy violations as defined in the system's content moderation rules.

Each article in the response includes the title, author display name, a snippet of flagged content, the reason code for the flag, and the timestamp of article creation. This allows administrators to quickly review potential violations without having to search through all articles. Only active articles (not deleted) are included. Articles flagged as "spam" or "irrelevant" but not requiring human review are excluded.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to administrators and super administrators only, as outlined in the permission matrix. Regular citizens cannot access this endpoint.

This endpoint complements the user-facing search functionality by providing a focused tool for content moderation teams to maintain a civil and evidence-based discourse environment.

Related Operations:
- GET /articles: Normal article browsing for all users
- POST /articles: User article creation
- PATCH /search/global: User-initiated search
- DELETE /articles/{id}: Administrator article deletion

responseBody.description: Paginated list of articles flagged for moderation review, including minimal content and flag reason.

operations.description:
Approve a previously flagged or pending comment in the moderation queue.

This endpoint allows super administrators to approve comments that have been flagged by users or automated systems for review. Once approved, the comment remains visible and active in the platform, and the approval action is logged in the audit trail. This operation is the counter-action to comment flags and is used to close moderation cases where content is determined to be appropriate.

When a comment is approved, it indicates that the system-wide moderation process has validated the comment as compliant with community guidelines. This does not modify the comment's content, author, or timestamps but changes its visibility status in moderation queues. Approved comments no longer appear in moderation dashboards requiring review.

The system does not maintain a dedicated approval field in the economic_board_comments table. Instead, approval actions are logged as administrative actions in the system audit trail. This ensures that the comment entity remains unchanged while providing a clear audit trail of moderation decisions.

This operation is designed to work seamlessly with the existing comment system and requires the calling user to have super administrator privileges. Regular administrators cannot approve comments via this endpoint.

Related operations:
- PATCH /moderation/comments/reject: For rejecting flagged comments
- DELETE /moderation/comments: For permanent deletion of comments
- GET /moderation/comments: For listing all pending flagged comments

This operation must be accompanied by a justification provided as part of the request body.
operations.name: approve

Create a new moderation audit record with action 'APPROVED', actor ID, timestamp, and justification. Do not modify the comment record itself. Clear any pending flag records associated with this comment. Return success confirmation with audit record ID.

requestBody.description: Used to approve a specific comment and provide justification for the moderation decision.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful approval and audit record details.

operations.description:
Reject a comment as a moderator, making it hidden from regular users while preserving it for audit purposes.

This operation allows administrators and super administrators to reject specific comments that violate community guidelines, platform policies, or content quality standards. The comment is not deleted; instead, its status is changed to 'rejected' with a reason provided by the moderator. Rejected comments remain in the database for auditing and appeal purposes but are no longer visible to regular users or in comment lists.

Rejection is distinct from deletion: rejected comments can be reviewed or appealed by super administrators, and the original content and author information are preserved. The rejection reason must be documented for accountability and transparency. This endpoint supports moderation workflows without compromising the integrity of the content history.

This operation requires the user to be authenticated as an administrator or super administrator. Unauthorized users will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden. Comment must exist and not already be rejected or deleted. Rejection reason must be provided and has a minimum length of 10 characters according to business rules.

Related operations: GET /moderation/comments/rejected (list all rejected comments), DELETE /comments/{id} (permanent deletion by super admin).

Validate that requester has administrator or superAdministrator role. Validate rejection_reason length (>=10 characters). Update comment with: deleted_by_admin = true, deletion_reason = @rejection_reason, deleted_at = current timestamp (Asia/Seoul). Return updated comment record. Log moderation action with admin ID, comment ID, and rejection reason in audit log.

requestBody.description: Rejection request containing comment identifier and reason for rejection.

responseBody.description: The comment record with updated rejection status and time.

Each record in the response includes the section name, the administrator's display name who created it, and the exact timestamp of creation. This information is presented in a summarized format optimized for listing interfaces, with full details available through associated links.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to super administrators due to the sensitive nature of administrative audit trails. This prevents misuse of administrative power by ensuring only the highest-level users can monitor other administrators' actions.

This operation complements the section management workflow, where section creation is an auditable administrative action. Users can verify that all sections were created by authorized personnel, and super administrators can identify patterns of activity or potential abuse.

Important: Section creation records are preserved in the audit log even if the corresponding section is later soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at). This endpoint provides a historical audit trail of all section deletion operations performed by administrators on the economic_board platform. Each audit record contains the section that was deleted, the administrator who performed the deletion, and the precise timestamp of the deletion event. This audit functionality ensures transparency and accountability in platform governance, allowing administrators to track when sections were removed and by whom.

The audit records are stored as immutable events in a dedicated audit table, independent of the original section records which are permanently removed upon deletion. This separation ensures the audit trail remains intact even after the original sections are deleted.

The response provides pagination support to handle potentially large volumes of deletion events that may accumulate over time. Only authenticated administrators and super administrators have access to this endpoint, as specified in the platform's security model.

Note: This endpoint returns audit records of section deletions only, not deletions of articles or comments. The system maintains separate audit trails for different types of administrative actions.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all user bans with associated administrator and citizen information.

This operation allows administrators to view the complete history of user bans, including the reason for each ban, the administrator who imposed it, and the duration of the ban. The list includes all ban records from the system's history, whether currently active or resolved. Active bans represent users who are permanently prohibited from accessing the service, while resolved bans indicate users whose access has been restored after the ban period has ended. Ban records are retained in the database for audit purposes, even when access has been restored, to maintain accountability and compliance.

Implementation note: This endpoint returns summary information only, linking to citizen.display_name and administrator.display_name for context, rather than full user objects to avoid circular dependencies and optimize response size. The bans are ordered by banned_at descending (newest first) and pagination is implemented using cursor-based counting to handle large datasets efficiently.

Security: Access is restricted to administrator roles only. Regular citizens will receive HTTP 403 Forbidden access.

Relationship to other operations: This endpoint complements the "GET /users" operation by providing context on account restrictions. It also supports the "POST /users/{id}/ban" operation by allowing administrators to review existing ban history before taking new actions.

Error handling: If the requesting user is not an administrator, the system returns HTTP 403 Forbidden. If the user is unauthorized to view bans, the operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized.

Include both active (unbanned_at IS NULL) and resolved (unbanned_at IS NOT NULL) bans in result set. Return count of total matches to support pagination controls. Do not return any actual citizen/administrator email addresses or password hashes. Only include required fields: id, citizen_display_name, administrator_display_name, ban_reason, banned_at, unbanned_at.
